transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-10 13:00 PST | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Nair, Diego Ramos, Leah Tan (Redwood) — Jordan Li, Maya Singh, Samir Patel, Olivia Chen, Evan Brooks (Vanguard)

00:00 Alex Kim: Okay, thanks everyone for joining on time. Quick agenda — run through the cutover playbook, dry-run the rollback steps, confirm canary metrics and alerts, and lock next steps. Is that good?
00:08 Jordan Li: Yep that's fine. We mostly want to make sure the rollback is clean — we had one incident in staging where the KV cache mismatch caused doubled tokens, so want to avoid that in prod.
00:20 Priya Nair: Got it, we'll call out the KV cache warming and prefix cache invalidation in the runbook. Diego will talk about the cache warming play.
00:30 Diego Ramos: Hi all. Quick note — we recommend a staged cache warm: first warm L0 on the canary nodes with a small corpus, watch memory and p50/p95, then expand. If you flood with large sequences you hit OOMs on older spine GPUs.
00:46 Maya Singh: Hey, what about the A/B approach? We were debating whether to do a weighted A/B or pure canary then full switch.
00:54 Alex Kim: Good question. For your traffic profile — mostly short prompts, lots of embeddings for search augmentation — we usually recommend a canary (1-2% of traffic) for 24 hours, then a 10% ramp if metrics stable, then 100% switch. A/B can work if you want model comparison, but it's more complex for cache and batching alignment.
01:12 Olivia Chen: If we do 1% canary, how does autoscale behave? Will the dedicated pool autoscale down and up and cause flapping?
01:20 Priya Nair: We set a min replica of 2 for canary so autoscale doesn't spin to zero. Also use burst capacity for warmups. We'll include explicit autoscale pins in the runbook.
01:34 Evan Brooks: For QA, we'll need a smoke test checklist. Can you include exact request patterns and token distributions? Last time the smoke test used 1k token prompts and didn't match real traffic.
01:45 Priya Nair: Yep, we'll attach a test traffic script — small, med, long — and we'll include a synthetic user journey with prefix caching to mirror real sessions.
01:56 Samir Patel: Security — quick interjection — during the canary we need to ensure no logs with PHI leak to Redwood. Are you able to mask or redaction at ingestion?
02:06 Alex Kim: Redwood's hosted offering has configurable redaction at the API gateway; for Dedicated or Private we can support customer-side redaction or model-side PII filters. We'll add a section in the playbook about log scrubbers and KMS for encrypted logs.
02:18 Jordan Li: Great. Let's step through the playbook. Priya?
02:22 Priya Nair: Sure. Slide one — pre-cutover checklist: verify SSO and service accounts, validate docker image hashes, confirm model variant (gptx-3.1-q4_0) pinned, smoke tests present, monitoring hooks in place, and rollback tag created. Also confirm access to the private control plane if you're on Private.
02:39 Jordan Li: We are on Dedicated, so control plane access is via our VPC peering. We'll double-check network ACLs.
02:46 Diego Ramos: For dedicated, also ensure that the GPU driver versions match the runtime matrix. Mismatched drivers can change kernel selection and perf variability.
02:56 Maya Singh: Can you explain the rollback tag? Is that a previous model or a config snapshot?
03:02 Priya Nair: It's both — we create a rollback deployment which is the previous stable model + pinned config. During cutover we keep it in standby and have a one-command rollback via orchestration that switches traffic back to the rollback deployment and triggers cache invalidation on the new nodes.
03:15 Alex Kim: Important caveat — rolling back model versions with different tokenizer or stateful layers can cause stale KV cache collisions. Our runbook recommends flush-and-warm on rollback nodes, not attempt partial reuse.
03:31 Olivia Chen: How long does a rollback typically take?
03:34 Priya Nair: If all artifacts are warmed, 3–5 minutes for traffic switch; if we need to reprovision instances it's more like 10–25 minutes depending on infra. We'll keep a 30-minute target for full recovery in the SLOs.
03:49 Jordan Li: Okay. Let's actually run a tabletop: dry-run scenario where the canary shows a p95 latency regression of +120ms and a slight increase in 5xxs. What's our play?
03:59 Alex Kim: Triage: 1) Abort ramp, 2) cut traffic back to 0 for canary, 3) if 5xx persists across old deployment then rollback to previous tag. We also snapshot traces and attach to the RCA. Priya will show the exact CLI commands.
04:16 Priya Nair: Command sequence: redwood ctl set-route weight pilot-route=0; redwood ctl deploy rollback --tag stable-2025-10-29; redwood ctl cache invalidate --scope new-nodes; Then run the smoke script and watch the dashboard.
04:33 Evan Brooks: Does the CLI handle draining in-flight tokens? We had users complain about truncated responses during a switch.
04:40 Priya Nair: We use a graceful drain flag — it waits up to X seconds for token service responses then force closes. We'll include recommended drain timeout (30s) in the runbook but you can bump to 60s if you prefer less truncation risk.
04:53 Samir Patel: Is audit logging preserved across the rollback? We need traceability for compliance.
04:58 Alex Kim: Yes, audit logs are append-only. Rollbacks and route changes are logged with user and timestamp and stored per your retention policy. We'll link to how to export logs to your SIEM.
05:12 Jordan Li: On monitoring — which specific metrics should we watch during the canary?
05:17 Priya Nair: Core metrics: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, token generation TPS, KV cache hit rate, GPU memory usage, batch size distribution, and queue length. Also model-quality deltas if you run eval prompts — we recommend a small set of golden prompts to track semantic regressions.
05:36 Maya Singh: For model-quality deltas, can we automate alerts if semantic similarity dips below threshold?
05:42 Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports automatic regression alerts based on prompt sets. We'll set a soft alert at 5% drop and a critical at 10%, but you can tune thresholds.
05:52 Olivia Chen: We want to avoid alert fatigue. Can we aggregate some of these into a single canary health score?
05:58 Diego Ramos: We can compute a composite score — weighted across latency, errors, and quality. We'll show a sample threshold in Grafana.
06:07 Alex Kim: Priya, can you show the Grafana canary dashboard mock?
06:12 Priya Nair: Sharing screen — okay you might see some fuzz from the screen share in the transcript. The top-left is throughput, top-right latency heatmap, mid-row is error rate and token efficiency, bottom is model-quality panel. We also added an annotation stream for deploy events.
06:29 Evan Brooks: Looks good. For the dry-run, we'll need sample alert thresholds. What's your recommended set?
06:34 Priya Nair: Suggested: p95 increase > 30% OR p95 > 600ms => warn; p95 increase > 60% OR p95 > 900ms => critical. For 5xx, warn at 0.5% and critical at 1.5%. For model-quality, warn at 5% drop, critical at 10%.
06:55 Jordan Li: Noted. Next — runbook roles. Who does what during cutover?
07:00 Alex Kim: Roles: Run lead (Vanguard has to assign, recommended Jordan), Redwood runbook engineer (Alex/Priya), SRE lead (Olivia), QA lead (Evan), Security lead (Samir). We'll include a RACI table in the doc.
07:14 Jordan Li: I can be run lead. I'll confirm after the call.
07:19 Samir Patel: I can be security lead. Two notes: we need to validate KMS key rotation window and ensure HSM policies are allowed for the rollback tag.
07:28 Alex Kim: We'll add the KMS checklist. Also, Leah from CS will coordinate the comms plan — how to notify internal stakeholders and customers during the dry-run.
07:37 Leah Tan: I'll draft an internal comms template and a blameless postmortem skeleton that the team can use.
07:44 Maya Singh: One technical concern — routing by policy. If we do region-based routing, can canary traffic be forced to a single region? We want consistent latency for the canary.
07:53 Priya Nair: Yes, route by region tag; we can pin canary instances to a single AZ to reduce variance. But that increases blast radius; tradeoff documented.
08:03 Olivia Chen: On the topic of canary duration — you recommended 24 hours earlier. For our compliance, we'd like a full working day. Can we set the primary canary for 8 hours then hold and evaluate?
08:12 Alex Kim: Absolutely, you can do an 8-hour canary then a decision gate. The runbook includes checklists for go/no-go at 1h, 4h, and 8h.
08:23 Jordan Li: Let's simulate the rollback now — dry-run verbally. Evan, pretend you hit the 'p95 +120ms and 5xx spike' and call it out.
08:33 Evan Brooks: (roleplay) Alert triggered: p95 increased 120ms, 5xxs at 0.9%.
08:38 Alex Kim: Action: Jordan hit abort ramp, Priya run warmdown command, Olivia watch drain. Jordan?
08:44 Jordan Li: Abort ramp — redwood ctl set-route weight pilot-route=0 — done.
08:48 Priya Nair: Running cache invalidate on new nodes — redwood ctl cache invalidate --scope new-nodes — done (dry-run).
08:56 Diego Ramos: Simulated rollback deploy — redwood ctl deploy rollback --tag stable-2025-10-29 — initiating.
09:03 Olivia Chen: Monitoring swarm — p95 should normalize as traffic returns to stable. Any action on the client side to prevent partial responses?
09:10 Priya Nair: We recommended client-side retry logic with idempotency keys; we'll include sample client pseudocode in the runbook.
09:18 Samir Patel: For the dry-run, what logs do we need to capture to validate cleanup?
09:23 Alex Kim: Capture deploy event logs, route change logs, cache invalidation logs, and traces for the 5xxs. Also collect GPU metrics and batch distribution snapshots. We'll provide a log export command.
09:34 Maya Singh: Sounds thorough. I have a question about darklaunching the new model for a subset of endpoints only — can we exclude endpoints that handle sensitive workflows?
09:42 Priya Nair: Yes, route-level config supports per-endpoint model pinning. You can keep sensitive endpoints on the stable tag and route experimental endpoints to the canary.
09:50 Jordan Li: One operational question — will the billing reflect canary usage? We want to confirm cost measurement during the POC.
09:56 Alex Kim: Yes, token-level billing is tracked per-route and we'll give a cost breakdown for canary vs baseline; Redwood Console shows per-route token counts and cost estimates. We'll share a sample cost report.
10:08 Evan Brooks: For the test traffic script, do you have a generator that can mock session state for prefix caching?
10:14 Priya Nair: Yes, we'll hand over a Python script that replays sessions with stateful prefixes — includes variable sequence lengths and user IDs to exercise KV caching.
10:22 Jordan Li: Perfect. Any last-minute compliance notes? Samir?
10:26 Samir Patel: Just the KMS rotation and audit export cadence. Also want to ensure RBAC restricts rollback capability to a small group.
10:34 Alex Kim: We recommend RBAC roles: deployer, runbook-operator (can trigger cutover/rollback), and observer. We'll provide recommended IAM policies.
10:44 Maya Singh: Timeline check — after the dry-run we want a short retro and then schedule the real cutover next week if all green.
10:50 Alex Kim: That works. Suggested dry-run date is 2025-11-18 as we discussed. We'll send calendar invite.
10:57 Jordan Li: I'll confirm the run lead and the 3-hour window by EOD Tuesday.
11:02 Leah Tan: I'll prepare comms templates and ship the runbook PDF once Alex shares the draft.
11:08 Alex Kim: Great — recap of deliverables: Alex share runbook; Priya share Grafana link and test script; Evan provide test script feedback; Samir provide compliance Qs. Anything else?
11:20 Maya Singh: Please include a short appendix with rollback times observed in your previous dedicated customers — ballpark numbers.
11:27 Priya Nair: We'll include anonymized rollbacks and timelines.
11:31 Jordan Li: Cool. Thanks everyone.
11:34 Alex Kim: Thanks — meeting adjourned.

Post-call notes: transcript has some auto-capture mis-hearings (e.g., redwood ctl typed commands may be condensed). Links shared in chat: runbook draft (link placeholder: https://redwood.example/runbooks/vanguard-cutover-draft), grafana canary template (https://grafana.example/d/abc123/canary-template), test-traffic script repo (https://git.example/vg-traffic-sim).
